messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: P1 latency spike for /v1/generate — error rate up, 95th latency > 3s for multiple customers. Paging oncall. https://ops.redwood/incidents/1787001234 :rotating_light:

maria (oncall): I'm on it. grabbing context from traces and logs. paging handoff to next in 30 if needed.

jonah: I'm available to assist — oncall-backup. any initial scope on impacted regions or model routes?

maria (oncall): Looks like US-west and EU-west. Preliminary metric: 5xx rate up from 0.2% -> 3.6% over last 6m. Model route `text-gen-llama-13b` hotspots in requests/sec.

sami (eng-sre): I'm seeing a lot of slow tail on the pods that route to the quantized variant. Could be kernel scheduling / batch growth. Pulling kube events now.

kyra (observability): FYI dashboards under `prod/latency` returning incomplete series for `route=text-gen-*`. Query returns partial because sampling on log-forwarder changed around 04:03 UTC. Investigating. :eyes: 

maria (oncall): opsbot, mute non-essential alerts for this thread.

opsbot: Acknowledged. Muting alert group: prod-latency-alerts for 60m.

jonah: Can someone paste the raw request logs for 04:00-04:10 UTC for a single affected pod? I want to see prefix / kv cache behavior.

sami (eng-sre): Pasting snippet from forwarded logs (redacted):

```
2026-03-14T04:05:12Z pod-ml-42 gen request id=abc123 route=text-gen-llama-13b seq=1 len=1024 latency_ms=3120 cache_hit=false
2026-03-14T04:05:12Z pod-ml-42 kernel: cuda context reset? errno=700
2026-03-14T04:05:13Z pod-ml-42 gen request id=abc124 route=text-gen-llama-13b seq=1 len=256 latency_ms=45 cache_hit=true
2026-03-14T04:05:14Z pod-ml-42 gen request id=abc125 route=text-gen-llama-13b seq=1 len=2048 latency_ms=4200 cache_hit=false
```

sami (eng-sre): We have interleaved high-latency and normal requests — suggests noisy neighbors or a batch shape problem. Also seeing some CUDA timeouts.

kyra (observability): OK big problem: our aggregated logs only show ~10% of requests in that time window — sampling rate was set to 0.1 by the log-forwarder change earlier today (whoops). That explains why dashboards looked 'clean' for many routes. Missing logs = blind spot.


taylor (support): Any idea how many customers were impacted? I'm getting DMs from two enterprise accounts complaining about slow responses. Need an ETA to tell them.

maria (oncall): Quick customer impact assessment: using traces we can see 12 customers hit >50% p95 degraded responses in last 10m; 3 customers have active errors. Detail followup after we stabilize.

jonah: Mitigation idea: fail traffic for `text-gen-llama-13b` to `text-gen-llama-7b` autoscale group as temporary fallback. It's compatible and lower mem so should avoid the kernel timeouts. Thoughts?

sami (eng-sre): +1 for fallback. Also rolling restart on the set of pods showing CUDA resets. I can do canary restarts of 2 pods to observe.

maria (oncall): I'm going to execute fallback route policy now. Will update when DNS/routing propagates.

incident-bot: ACTION: routing-rule updated by maria (oncall) — fallback enabled: text-gen-llama-13b -> text-gen-llama-7b.

maria (oncall): Fallback enabled. Noticeable drop in 95th latency in the last 2m for US-west: from 3100ms -> 220ms approx. Errors decreasing.

kyra (observability): Able to run ad-hoc query against raw traces (but remember sampling blind spots). Query I ran:

```
SELECT service, route, percentile(latency_ms, 95) as p95
FROM traces
WHERE ts BETWEEN 1678790400000 AND 1678791000000
GROUP BY service, route
ORDER BY p95 DESC
LIMIT 20
```
kyra (observability): Result shows the `text-gen-llama-13b` peak, and fallback `llama-7b` already absorbing traffic. However the total request count we see is 12% of expected due to forwarding sampling.

jonah: Can we increase sampling to 1.0 and re-ingest for the last 20m? We need full logs for the RCA timeline.

kyra (observability): I don't think we can retroactively re-ingest external telemetry from the forwarder if it never forwarded. But we can turn sampling to 1.0 going forward and pull from the retention buffer for a short window (we have ~30m of raw buffer). I'll enable it now.

opsbot: Sampling config change detected: log-forwarder sampling_rate=1.0 by kyra (observability).

sami (eng-sre): I started canary restarts on pod-ml-{42,43}. Observing kernel logs during restart...

sami (eng-sre): Kernel logs show repeated GPUDRV errors around the time of spike: `NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:01:00): 79` — indicative of driver/oom? Also memory pressure spikes on node host.

maria (oncall): Running `kubectl top node` shows one node with +80% mem and high GPU util. Could be batch packing causing long-lived big tensors.

jonah: Hypothesis 1: a recent model quantization change increased memory footprint when serving certain sequence lengths, causing OOM/driver resets under batch pressure.

jonah: Hypothesis 2: autoscaler policy misconfigured — aggressive batching increased effective batch size for mixed workloads, causing tail latency.

maria (oncall): Hypothesis 3: log-forwarder sampling change masked the early signal so autoscaling didn't react in time.

kyra (observability): Adding to thread hypotheses and timeline. We still need the edge-case request payloads for sequences >1024 to prove hypothesis 1. Can we get a sample payload?

sami (eng-sre): Found one in retained-forwarder buffer, redacted payload below:

```
{ "id": "abc125", "route": "text-gen-llama-13b", "input_len": 2048, "prompt": "<redacted>" }
```

maria (oncall): Good. That maps to the big-len requests in logs. I'm going to scale up the `llama-13b` pool with temporarily higher node count and add a strict batch size cap (max_batch_tokens=1024) while we stabilize.

sami (eng-sre): Implemented batch cap change in runtime config (canary) and scaled +2 nodes on the pool.

opsbot: Runtime config change applied: max_batch_tokens=1024 (canary).

maria (oncall): After scale + batch cap, p95 normalized further, 5xxs falling. Starting timeline write-up:
1) 03:58 UTC - log-forwarder sampling lowered to 0.1 (deploy) -> reduced observability
2) 04:01 UTC - model rollout with quantization tweak to 13b (small percent)
3) 04:03 UTC - tail latency begins; dashboards looked partial due to sampling
4) 04:05 UTC - kernel timeouts and CUDA errors on several pods
5) 04:08 UTC - fallback routing enabled -> immediate improvement
6) 04:15 UTC - sampling restored; canary restarts & batch cap applied; full stabilization by 04:35

jonah: That timeline looks right. We'll capture precise request counts and affected customer list in the RCA doc.


taylor (support): Noted. I informed the three impacted enterprise customers that we have mitigation and will follow up with a detailed RCA.

kyra (observability): Observability gaps action items:
- Prevent sampling changes in prod without a rollout tag and dependency check (blocker)
- Ensure critical routes (`text-gen-*`) are always unsampled or have minimum sampling=1.0
- Add dashboard alert to detect sudden drop in log ingestion / sampling delta

maria (oncall): Agreed. We'll open tickets for each. Also: we need an immediate short-term playbook update for oncall to check sampling config when latency spikes look absent in dashboards.

sami (eng-sre): I'll open an ops-ticket for driver team to check GPU firmware/driver stability on the affected node pool. Also will revert the quantization rollout to stable previous image for now.

maria (oncall): Can everyone add their notes to the incident doc at https://docs.redwood/incidents/1787001234-rca-merge ? We'll do a formal postmortem after 24h.

incident-bot: Incident P1 acknowledged as mitigated, status: partial-blameless RCA in progress.

maria (oncall): Handoff to next oncall (jonah) in 30m for post-incident monitoring and RCA follow-up. Thanks all. :heart:

jonah: Taking handoff. Will coordinate RCA items and follow ups.

kyra (observability): Follow-up immediate PRs: set `critical_routes_unsampled = true` in forwarder config, add sampling delta alert. ETA PR today.

sami (eng-sre): Follow-ups: rollback quantization rollout, schedule GPU driver health check, add canary batch cap test.

maria (oncall): Closing incident channel for active mitigation — leave comments in the doc.
